title: On Aligning Tuples for Regression

problem.claim: Regression requires values collected separately from multiple variables to be aligned into tuples before model learning.

gap.claim: Timestamp-based concatenation yields limited learning data, while existing time-series matching methods rely on value and timestamp similarity that may be absent across regression variables.

contributions.claim: The paper formulates tuple alignment under time and model constraints and proves the problem is NP-complete.
The paper devises an approximation algorithm with a performance guarantee for constrained tuple alignment.
The paper proposes efficient pruning strategies for its alignment algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets, including engine data from a vehicle manufacturer, report improved alignment accuracy and regression precision over existing methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Regression models combine multiple variables, whose separately collected values must be aligned into tuples.
Recording delays and timestamp differences make straightforward alignment difficult and reduce usable learning data.
Existing matching techniques depend on similarities that may not exist between regression variables.
The paper aligns variable values within a short time period while requiring compatibility with the regression model.
The authors report theoretical contributions, algorithmic techniques, and improved alignment accuracy and regression precision in experiments.

source_observation.claim: When variables are collected independently and timestamp similarity is unavailable, alignment can be defined using both temporal proximity and compatibility with the downstream regression model.

interpretation.claim: Data alignment may need to optimize for the requirements of the eventual learning task rather than relying only on generic similarity.

application.claim: For multi-sensor regression pipelines, consider task-aware tuple construction with explicit time constraints and model constraints.

exception.claim: This lesson may not apply when variables have reliable synchronized timestamps or meaningful cross-variable value similarity.

unknowns: The specific model constraint and regression formulation are not given.
The approximation guarantee and pruning strategy details are not given.
Dataset counts, evaluation metrics, and experimental conditions are not given.
